svg.text: The two most-solved proteins on Earth are both from one virus
anyone reading deposition volume as the field's capacity
whether a busy year is more structural biology or one subject
the SARS-CoV-2 targets fall away after 2021 like a news cycle
the target list is an ordinary power law
rank against entries, both on log scales — a straight line means a power law
rank among the 200 most-solved proteins (log scale)
The 200 most-solved proteins carry 95,377 entity-entries. The distribution
is an unremarkable power law and the replicase sits only 1.6x above it — so
the notable thing about the head of this list is which proteins are in it,
not how far they stand out. A count of entries is a count of attention: the
same protein re-solved with a different ligand is two entries.
and the virus did not go away
depositions per year for the top targets
The spike peaked in 2022 and fell away. The replicase polyprotein did not —
it was still drawing 582 depositions in 2024, because that polyprotein
contains the main protease and the field is doing antiviral chemistry
against it. Every grey line is a classic target running flat underneath.
RCSB PDB search API, fetched 2026-09-22, grouped on the UniProt accession of the polymer entity. An accession is one polymer and an entry with several
distinct chains appears under each, so these are entity-entries and cannot be added across accessions to recover an entry count — the same
multi-valued trap as the author facet in figure 2. Deposition date throughout. The facet returns the 200 largest, so the tail beyond rank 200 is not
drawn and no Gini or cumulative share is computed from a truncated list. It also returns them — 35 of the 200 — out of count order, so they are sorted
here before anything is called a rank; the earlier version of this figure did not, which moved the fit from R² 0.77 to 0.88.
